Hi Jordan / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Sparkplug is excited about the performance numbers. Legal asked me to send over our standard DPA redlines and our current subprocessor list. Heads up on two asks that are blocking procurement on our side:

1) We need a clause that prevents the provider from using customer data to train models (all training/data-use prohibited).
2) We want the ability to review and approve any new subprocessor with a 30-day notice; for existing subprocessors we expect an explicit inventory and assurance that certain analytics vendors are not used for raw telemetry.

I attached: Sparkplug_DPA_redline_v3.docx and Sparkplug_subprocessor_list_20270810.xlsx. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a training prohibition and provide the subprocessor inventory with technical notes on telemetry exports? We aim to close the contract this month.

Jordan / all — thanks, I reviewed Sparkplug_DPA_redline_v3 and their subprocessor inventory. High-level legal stance: we should try to accommodate commercial customers but not at expense of core infra ops. Specific notes:

- Training prohibition: We can agree to a narrow clause prohibiting using their identifiable customer content for model training or for improvements that would make outputs attributable to that customer. We want to preserve our ability to use aggregated, de-identified signals for product quality and model tuning. Proposed compromise language in attached redline: "Provider shall not use Customer Content in a manner that associates such content with Customer for model training; Provider may use de-identified and aggregated telemetry for system improvement provided such data cannot be reconstructed to identify Customer."

- Subprocessors & 30-day approval: 30-day approval for each new subprocessor is operationally difficult. Standard is notice with opt-out for a short window for high-risk categories. Suggested path: 1) provide Sparkplug the current inventory and classify high-risk vendors (security/analytics). 2) For new subprocessors, provide 30-day notice and allow for a remediation discussion; only for high-risk categories require explicit written approval.

- Telemetry vendors: their list calls out an analytics vendor we use for aggregated metrics (CloudPulse). We need Product ops to confirm CloudPulse only receives aggregated metrics and not raw prompts/responses.

I attached a legal redline (redline_comments_jb.docx) that aligns with these points. Once Product and Security confirm the technical constraints we can send a counter-redline.

Olga Petrov
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DPA redlines from Sparkplug — product impact and recommended wording

Thanks for the clear summary, Olga. Quick product/ops take:

- Training prohibition: Technically feasible to ensure customer prompts/responses are not used for model training or fine-tuning if we apply strict tagging and isolation at inference ingress and block retention for those tenants. That will increase storage/retention complexity and slightly increase per-request latency due to additional classification steps, but acceptable for named enterprise deals. We should estimate a 1-2% latency increase under current load shapes and plan for the onboarding checklist to set "no-training" for the tenant.

- Telemetry/CloudPulse: Confirmed — CloudPulse receives aggregated metrics only (60s rollups, no raw prompt/response payloads). The analytics pipeline has a KV-cache snapshot job for debugging; we can ensure Sparkplug is excluded from KV snapshots and restrict debug dumps behind a documented on-call approval.

Recommended contract language (short):
"Provider shall not use Customer Content for model training or fine-tuning. Provider may use aggregated and de-identified telemetry for system performance monitoring and product improvement; Provider shall exclude Customer from any KV-cache snapshot exports and shall require documented, time-limited on-call approval for any debug exports that include content-level artifacts."

If Legal is comfortable with 'aggregated and de-identified' carveout and Security signs off on the debug export control, Product can accept. We should also include onboarding steps in the SOW to configure the tenant properly.

Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: DPA redlines from Sparkplug — security conditions for signoff

All — quick security assessment and conditional sign-off. I reviewed Olga's proposed compromise and Laura's operational mitigations. We can accept the proposed language with these non-negotiable security conditions to be included in the DPA or Exhibit B: 

1) Provider maintains SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent) and provides evidence annually (report or AOC).
2) Provider commits to annual external penetration testing with remediation timelines and will provide a summary report to Sparkplug under NDA.
3) Customer data must be encrypted at rest and in transit; for customers who require it we will offer a dedicated KMS key (bring-your-own-key) option and document how keys are scoped per-tenant.
4) Any debug/KV-cache export requires documented justification, approval by security on-call, and must be stored in encrypted form with retention not exceeding 30 days.

If Legal includes the above, Security gives signoff and Product's operational constraints (no-KV-snapshot for Sparkplug; tagging at ingress) are acceptable. Olga — please confirm you can fold these bullets into our counter-redline; Jordan — I recommend we send the counter with a one-pager and offer a 30-minute call to finalize.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Privacy | Redwood Inference
